findings.title: Credentials sent in cleartext
evidence: LOGIN for user 'ananya.sharma@example.com' (accepted); password/token crossed the wire unencrypted (secret not stored)
findings.remediation: Refuse authentication before TLS: Postfix `smtpd_tls_auth_only = yes`; Dovecot `disable_plaintext_auth = yes` / `auth_allow_cleartext = no`. Rotate the exposed credentials listed in the evidence - they must be assumed compromised.

findings.title: STARTTLS vanished versus endpoint baseline - possible active MITM
evidence: endpoint offered TLS in 7 of 7 baseline sessions; this session: capability absent
EHLO capability 'XXXXXXXX' is a same-length rewrite of STARTTLS
findings.remediation: Treat as a potential active interception: preserve this capture (hash recorded in the report), trace the network path between the client and the server (ARP/DHCP/DNS spoofing, rogue gateway, compromised middlebox), and verify the server's real certificate out-of-band. Long term: MTA-STS enforce / DANE for relays, implicit TLS with certificate validation for clients.
compliance: CERT-In Directions 28 Apr 2022 (attack on mail server: report within 6 h)

findings.title: STARTTLS stripping indicators
evidence: EHLO capability 'XXXXXXXX' is a same-length rewrite of STARTTLS
capabilities seen: PIPELINING SIZE XXXXXXXX AUTH ENHANCEDSTATUSCODES 8BITMIME DSN
findings.remediation: Move clients to implicit TLS (465 / 993 / 995, RFC 8314): there is no cleartext upgrade to strip. Postfix submission: `smtpd_tls_security_level = encrypt`, `smtpd_tls_auth_only = yes`. Dovecot: `ssl = required` and `disable_plaintext_auth = yes` (2.4: `auth_allow_cleartext = no`). Set mail clients to 'TLS required', never 'STARTTLS if available'.
compliance: CERT-In Directions 28 Apr 2022 (attack on mail server: report within 6 h)

findings.title: STARTTLS command/response injection
evidence: client sent 41 bytes of cleartext after STARTTLS before TLS (pipelined commands: RSET, MAIL)
findings.remediation: Upgrade the server/client: the implementation must discard any buffered plaintext when TLS starts (CVE-2011-0411 class; 40+ implementations affected per Poddebniak et al. 2021). Check Postfix, Dovecot, Exim, Courier versions; prefer implicit TLS ports which have no upgrade step.
compliance: CERT-In Directions 28 Apr 2022 (attack on mail server: report within 6 h)
references: USENIX Security 2021: Why TLS is better without STARTTLS

findings.title: STARTTLS stripping indicators
evidence: STARTTLS refused with '454 4.7.0 TLS not available due to local problem'
capabilities seen: PIPELINING SIZE VRFY ETRN STARTTLS ENHANCEDSTATUSCODES 8BITMIME DSN SMTPUTF8 CHUNKING
findings.remediation: Publish an MTA-STS policy in `mode: enforce` (RFC 8461) and/or DANE TLSA records (RFC 7672) so sending MTAs refuse to deliver without TLS. On Postfix senders use `smtp_tls_security_level = dane` (or `encrypt`/`verify` per destination via `smtp_tls_policy_maps`). Inspect the network path: a same-length rewrite of the capability is the signature of an inline stripping device or compromised middlebox.

findings.title: Server does not offer STARTTLS
findings.remediation: Enable TLS and make it mandatory: Postfix `smtpd_tls_security_level = encrypt`; Dovecot `ssl = required`. Prefer implicit TLS ports 465/993/995 (RFC 8314) and close 110/143 to clients.

findings.title: Server selected a cipher suite the client did not offer
evidence: client offered 12 suites, not including it
a conforming server cannot do this; the ServerHello did not come from the client's peer
findings.remediation: A conforming server cannot answer outside what the client offered, so treat this as a possible in-path device rewriting the handshake. Capture again from the same tap point, compare against a capture taken adjacent to the server, and audit any TLS-inspecting proxy or load balancer between the two hosts.

findings.title: Downgrade sentinel present
evidence: ServerHello.random ends with DOWNGRD marker (TLS1.2) while negotiating TLS 1.2
findings.remediation: A TLS 1.3-capable server negotiated a lower version and signalled it (RFC 8446 §4.1.3). Check the client's TLS library and any middlebox on the path; enable TLS 1.3 end to end.
compliance: NIST SP 800-52 Rev. 2 §3.1 (TLS 1.2 minimum, TLS 1.3 support)

findings.title: Weak certificate key (RSA 1024)
findings.remediation: Reissue with RSA >= 2048 bits or ECDSA P-256.

findings.title: Obsolete protocol TLS 1.0
evidence: TLS 1.0 is deprecated by RFC 8996 (BEAST, no AEAD suites, SHA-1/MD5 PRF)
findings.remediation: Postfix: `smtpd_tls_protocols = >=TLSv1.2` and `smtpd_tls_mandatory_protocols = >=TLSv1.2` (same for `smtp_` on the client side). Dovecot: `ssl_min_protocol = TLSv1.2`.
compliance: NIST SP 800-52 Rev. 2 §3.1 (TLS 1.2 minimum, TLS 1.3 support)

findings.title: Weak cipher suite TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA
findings.remediation: Postfix: `smtpd_tls_mandatory_ciphers = high`, `smtpd_tls_exclude_ciphers = aNULL, eNULL, EXPORT, RC4, 3DES, MD5, DES, IDEA`, `tls_preempt_cipherlist = yes`. Dovecot: `ssl_cipher_list = ECDHE+AESGCM:ECDHE+CHACHA20:DHE+AESGCM:!aNULL:!MD5:!RC4:!3DES`, `ssl_prefer_server_ciphers = yes`.

findings.title: Weak Diffie-Hellman group (1024 bits)
findings.remediation: Use a 2048-bit or larger DH group (`openssl dhparam -out dh2048.pem 2048`; Postfix `smtpd_tls_dh1024_param_file = /etc/postfix/dh2048.pem`, Dovecot `ssl_dh = </etc/dovecot/dh.pem`) or drop DHE in favour of ECDHE.

findings.title: Client ignored offered STARTTLS
evidence: server advertised STARTTLS; client continued with EHLO, MAIL, RCPT, DATA, QUIT
findings.remediation: Server offered STARTTLS but the client did not use it. Configure the client (or sending MTA: `smtp_tls_security_level = may` at minimum) to always upgrade; for submission/access require TLS server-side so the client cannot proceed in cleartext.

findings.title: Certificate does not chain to a trusted root
evidence: a certificate in the path was outside its validity window at capture time, so the path could not be built
findings.remediation: Use a certificate chaining to a trusted root, or distribute the private CA to all clients / use DANE.
compliance: PCI DSS 4.0 Req. 4.2.1 (certificates valid, not expired)

findings.title: No forward secrecy
evidence: all recorded sessions become decryptable if the server private key is ever exposed
findings.remediation: Prefer ECDHE key exchange: put ECDHE suites first and remove static-RSA suites (`smtpd_tls_exclude_ciphers = kRSA` in Postfix; `!kRSA` in Dovecot `ssl_cipher_list`).

formulas.name: Finding risk
formulas.expr: 100 x severity x exposure x (0.5 + 0.5 x exploitability) x criticality
formulas.note: Ranks one finding against another. Severity is what is wrong; risk is how much it matters here. A medium on a submission port outranks a high on an internal relay, which is the whole point of separating them.

formulas.name: Session rule risk
formulas.expr: 100 x (1 - product over findings of (1 - severity x (0.6 + 0.4 x exploitability)))
formulas.note: Noisy-OR. Several mediums accumulate but can never exceed one critical, so a session cannot be pushed to the top by sheer count of small issues.

formulas.name: Session risk (with the model)
formulas.expr: 0.6 x rule risk + 0.4 x model risk, +10 if flagged as an outlier (capped at 100)
formulas.note: The model adjusts a rule-derived score; it never produces one alone. With --no-ml the rule risk is used unchanged.

formulas.name: Posture score
formulas.expr: 100 - sum of penalties over unique (rule, endpoint) pairs; capped at 59 if any critical
formulas.note: Deduplicating by (rule, endpoint) stops one noisy server from sinking the capture twice. The cap exists because a grade above F next to a critical finding would be read as 'broadly fine', which it is not.

scoring.exposure_note: Submission and access carry user credentials and mailbox content; a relay carries mail but no user password. Traffic private at both ends is discounted by a further 0.8.
not_scored: Revocation: a passive capture holds no OCSP or CRL response unless the server stapled one.
TLS 1.3 certificates: the Certificate message is encrypted, so none is recovered or assumed.
Message content: never parsed, never stored, and not an input to any score.
Hops outside the capture: a tap sees the hops that crossed it and no others.
